correctness.rationale: The proof starts from four general points in P^3 whose projected image is a reduced (2,2) complete intersection. The standard zero-dimensional complete-intersection coordinate-ring regularity is Σ(d_i-1), giving surjectivity of degree N-1 evaluation when N-1 ≥ that sum. For p≥3, the induction type in P^m is (2,2,p,...,p^(m-3)) and reg=2+Σ_{i=1}^{m-3}(p^i-1) ≤ p^(m-2)-1; hence the stated Artin--Schreier lifting theorem appends p^(m-2). For p=2, reg of (2,2,4,...,2^(m-2)) is 2^(m-1)-m+1 ≤2^(m-1)-1, appending 2^(m-1). Base case p≥3 uses p-1≥2, and p=2 starts with N=4. Product of CI degrees proves both cardinality formulas. Positionwise comparison against the (3,p,p²,...) and (3,4,8,...) published types is strictly smaller for every n≥4. The independent argument is conditional on the primary Theorem 4.2's exact evaluation-map hypothesis; a bounded verifier is not the geometric proof.
